draft.title: Popular culture and identity
card: Identity is how a person sees themselves and how others see them. Popular culture gives people ways to show it.
a person shows who they are through what they choose, such as the music they play, the clothes they wear or the games they stream.
sharing a taste in popular culture can link people to a group, such as fans of a band or a sport. Wearing a team jersey or joining an online fan page marks a person as part of that group.
People may use popular culture to express identity and to belong, and a person can belong to more than one group at once.
draft.remember: People can use popular culture to show who they are and to link themselves to others.

a.q: Dani wears her netball club's jersey to school and joins the club's online fan page. Which is the best description of what she is doing?
opts: Expressing her identity and showing she belongs to a group
Expressing her identity but not belonging to any group
Showing she belongs to a group but not expressing identity
Following a taste that has no link to who she is
a.why: The jersey shows what Dani cares about, which is expression. The fan page links her to other supporters, which is belonging. The other options split the two ideas apart, but a single choice can do both.
a.clue: Ask what she shows about herself and who she links up with.

b.q: Sam has listened to hip hop for years and now goes to gigs with friends who share that taste. How does this show a link between popular culture and identity?
opts: His music taste helps him express himself and join a group
His friends were chosen for him by the music industry
His music taste means he cannot belong to other groups
His music taste is shared by everyone in his school
b.why: Sam's taste in music expresses who he is, and the gigs link him to friends with the same taste. The card says a person can belong to more than one group, so his taste does not shut out other groups. Nothing suggests everyone at his school shares it.
b.clue: Look for the option that covers both showing who he is and fitting in with others.

a.best: Expressing her identity and showing she belongs to a group

b.best: His music taste helps him express himself and join a group

problems.detail: The clue ('Look for the option that covers both showing who he is and fitting in with others') nearly names the right option, so a student can pick it without understanding the idea.
The clue points to both expression and belonging, which leaves only the option that combines the two. It largely gives the answer away.

The wrong options (the music industry choosing his friends, everyone at school sharing his taste, being unable to belong to other groups) are implausible, so the question is too easy for Year 12 HSC students.

proposal.title: Popular culture and identity
card: Identity is how a person sees themselves and how others see them. Popular culture gives people ways to show it.

b.q: Sam wears hip hop fashion, goes to gigs with friends who share his taste and supports a rugby league team with his family. What does this show?
opts: His choices express who he is and link him to two groups
He can belong to only one group, so he must pick one
His gigs show belonging, so they cannot express identity
His identity is only how he sees himself, not others
b.why: Sam's clothes and music express who he is, and the gigs and the team link him to two groups. A person can belong to more than one group, so he does not have to pick one. One choice can both express identity and show belonging, and identity includes how others see him.
